_readme: Evaluation set for Week 5 hybrid retrieval: 15 queries over the 50-paper arXiv cs.CL corpus.
GROUND TRUTH IS LABELLED AT CHUNK LEVEL (`relevant_chunk_ids`). Paper-level relevance is
derived from it in the evaluation script (a chunk_id is '<paper_id>_<n>'), so the same 15
queries are scored at both granularities and the two numbers are directly comparable.
Why chunk level. An earlier version of this set labelled whole papers and every method scored
an identical 83.3% Hit@3 -- the task was saturated. The corpus has 50 papers on 50 essentially
disjoint topics, so any signal at all identifies the right paper, and because a paper's chunks
cluster together in both rankings, top-3 almost always contains one. Chunk level asks the
question RAG actually needs answered: not 'which paper' but 'which passage do I put in the
prompt'. The paper-level scores are still reported, as evidence for exactly this point.
How the queries were written. For each target paper the full chunk list was read, a specific
technical detail was picked, and the query was written to ask about that detail. A chunk is
listed as relevant only if it actually contains the answer -- several queries have more than
one because the corpus genuinely repeats a fact across chunks. Labels were fixed before any
retrieval was run against them, and no query was reworded after seeing a method's score.
Interference groups are deliberate: 2608.08082/2608.08086 are both masked-diffusion-LM papers,
2608.08168/2608.07852 both apply sparse autoencoders. Retrieving the right paper of a pair is
not enough; the right passage inside it still has to win.
`type` splits the set three ways:
semantic - paraphrase, deliberately avoiding the passage's own vocabulary; favours vectors
keyword  - literal identifiers and coined names present in the passage; favours BM25
mixed    - a named entity plus surrounding concepts; the case fusion should win

queries.note: Three literal system names that occur in exactly one chunk of the MoE survey.

queries.query: replicating hotspot experts at runtime to avoid device stragglers
queries.note: DeepSeek-V3 redundant expert deployment. 'hotspot' and 'stragglers' are literal; the framing is conceptual.

queries.query: why do some experts stop receiving training signal when only a few are picked per token
queries.note: Answer is 'Top-k causes unselected experts to have no gradient'. Query avoids 'Top-k', 'gradient', 'capacity'.

queries.query: All-to-All metadata and small-GEMM fragmentation when experts get too few tokens
queries.note: Literal technical terms from one chunk of the survey, plus the conceptual condition.

queries.query: once a position has been filled in it can never be revised, so what repair is left
queries.note: Answer: reopening is the only repair under absorbing unmasking. Query avoids 'reopening', 'absorbing', 'masked'.

queries.query: commitment horizon definition tolerance epsilon earliest persistent switch point
queries.note: Definition 1 of the CFG paper. Interference: 2608.08086 is the other diffusion-LM paper.

queries.query: Archer refresh when Hamming distance to the anchor exceeds K
queries.note: The state-aware refresh rule, stated in exactly one chunk.

queries.query: how much quality and speed does reusing cached states buy on code generation benchmarks
queries.note: Answer: Pass@1 up to 3.05 points, 1.36-1.78x speedup on MBPP/LiveCodeBench. Query avoids all of those literals.

queries.query: insertion strategy beginning only end only number of inserted embeddings
queries.note: The PEP ablation over prompt-embedding insertion positions.

queries.query: spotting untruthful answers by reading a frozen network's internal activations
queries.note: Paraphrase of hidden-state hallucination detection; both the abstract chunk and the intro chunk state it. Interference: 2608.07525 and 2608.08180 are also hallucination papers.

queries.query: k-sparse autoencoders avoid the shrinkage bias of L1 regularization
queries.note: Interference: 2608.07852 also uses sparse autoencoders, but on personas, and does not discuss shrinkage bias.

queries.query: which mode leans on worded-out logical connectives and which leans on mathematical symbols
queries.note: Thinking vs NoThinking token-composition contrast. Query avoids 'Thinking', 'NoThinking', 'reasoning tokens'.

queries.query: pushing a model out of an assigned character and back to its ordinary helper voice
queries.note: Negative steering returns the Assistant to default mode. Query avoids 'steering', 'persona', 'Assistant', 'roleplay'.

queries.query: do models tackle exam questions in the order shown rather than by how many marks they carry
queries.note: Answer: allocation is governed by presentation order, not point values. Query avoids 'presentation position', 'point values', 'allocation'.

queries.query: top-density overlap and early-position overlap of the work set
queries.note: Two coined metric names defined in exactly one chunk.
